sentences.text: JUDGMENT

The complainant filed the complaint under Section 223 Bharathiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act.
2.

The brief case of the complainant is as under:
That complainant is running real estate business in the name and style 'COEVOLVE ESTATES PVT. LTD' and accused being known to the complainant, the accused along with two others approached the complainant to purchase converted land bearing Sy.No.193/1 measuring 2 acre 5 guntas and 193/2 measuring 2 acre 5 guntas situated at Channappanahalli, Kolar Taluk and District.
After negotiation, the complainant executed sale deed dated05.09.2024 in favour of the accused and in favour of N.Venugopalreddy and Mr.G.A.Muniraju for total sale consideration of Rs.4,45,50,000/-.

At the time of execution of registered sale deed, out of total sale consideration of Rs.4,45,50,000/- accused issued 2 post dated cheques ie cheque bearing No.004729 dated 25.02.2025 for a sum of Rs.61,37,500/- and cheque bearing No.004730 dated C.C.No.19265/2025 25.02.2025 for a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- drawn on Union Bank, Bangalore in favour of the complainant.

The complainant presented both cheques through its banker i.e. Axis Bank, Koramangala,
Bangalore and both cheques returned dishonored on 04-03-2025 for the reason "Funds Insufficient".
The complainant informed the same to the accused and then accused has given a letter seeking time to arrange funds.
The complainant again presented both cheques on 02.04.2025 through its banker and said cheques again came to be returned dishonored for the reason "Funds Insufficient" vide memo dated 03.04.2025.

That the accused requested for one more week and the complainant believing the words of accused, presented said cheque on 19.04.2025 through his banker ie Axis Bank, Koramangala,
Bangalore, said cheque returned with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient" on 21.04.2025.

Hence,
the complainant got issued legal notice dated 06.05.2025 and called upon to pay the amount covered under both the cheques and the said notice returned with shara "Addressee Refused" on 09.05.2025.
Inspite of service of notice, the accused failed to pay the claim amount to the complainant with in the statutory time.
Therefore, the accused has committed the offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Therefore the complainant has filed the complaint.

On the basis of Private complaint filed by the complainant, this court has taken cognizance of offence and registered the case in PCR No.8721/2025 and recorded sworn statement of the authorised representative of complainant as PW 1 and got marked 16 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.16.

The accused has pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

sentences.text: As the evidence of complainant is already on record, the incriminating circumstances in the evidence of complainant is read over to the accused and his statement C.C.No.19265/2025 under Section 351 of BNSS has been recorded.
The accused has denied the incriminating circumstances as false.
The accused has filed application to recall of PW 1 and the same is allowed and PW 1 was recalled.

When the case is posted for cross examination of PW 1, the complainant and accused appeared before this court and have filed joint memo stating that they have arrived at amicable settlement in respect of payment of due amount by the accused and requested to pass judgment and consider the joint memo for awarding fine and compensation.

6. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the complainant and learned counsel for the accused and perused the material on record.
7.

On the basis of the material on record the following points arise for the consideration of this court :
1.

Whether the complainant proves beyond reasonable doubt that the accused issued cheque bearing No. 004729 for a sum of Rs.61,37,500/- and cheque bearing No.004730 for Rs.50,00,000/- both dated 25.02.2025 drawn on Union Bank of India, Singahalli branch, Bangalore in favour of the complainant towards discharge of legal liability and both the cheques dishonored on 21.04.2025 for the reason "Funds Insufficient" and C.C.No.19265/2025 inspite of service of legal notice dated 06.05.2025 accused has not complied the same within statutory time and thus committed an offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act ?
2. Whether the joint memo filed by both the complainant and the accused can be considered for imposing fine and awarding compensation ?
3. What Order?
8.

 Point No.1&2 In the Affirmative.

sentences.text:
The essential ingredients of section 138 and 142 of Negotiable Instruments Act to be complied are i) drawing of the cheque by the accused ii) presentation of the cheque to the bank with in the period of three months, iii) returning of the cheque unpaid by the drawee bank iv) giving notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque demanding of the payment of cheque amount with in the period of 30 days, v) failure of the drawer to make payment within the period of 15 days after receipt of the demand notice and v) Presentation of the complaint within a month by the complainant after expiry of 15 days of service of notice to the accused.
12.
The PW 1 has deposed that the accused issued 2 cheques ie cheque bearing No.004729 for rs.61,37,500/- and cheque bearing No. 004730 for Rs.50,00,000/- dated 25.02.2025 drawn on Union Bank, Bangalore.
Said Cheques were dishonoured for the reasons "Funds Insufficient" in the account of the accused on 21-04-2025 as per EX.P 9 and 10.

As provided under Section 146 of Negotiable Instruments Act law presumes that on production of banker slip or memo having thereon the official mark denoting that the cheque has been dishonored, presume the fact of dishonor of such said cheque, unless and until same is disproved.
The PW1 has deposed that they have got issued legal notice dated 06.05.2025 calling upon the accused to pay the amount involved in the cheques as per C.C.No.19265/2025 Ex.P11.
The notice returned on 09.05.2025 with an endorsement "Addressee Refused".
The notice is issued to the same address mentioned in the sale deed executed by the accused as Ex.P 14.
As the notice is returned as refused, it is presumed that the accused is fully aware of the notice and intentionally got it returned as refused.
Hence, the notice is deemed to be served.
Therefore the cause of action arose on expiry of 15 days of service of notice on 25-05-2025.
The complaint is filed before this court on 13.06.2025.
The cheque is presented through the account of the complainant with Axis Bank Koramangala, which is situated with in the jurisdiction of this court.
Thus the complainant has complied all the statutory requirements for constitution of offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Therefore, the complainant is entitled for presumption under Section 139 of Negotiable Instrument Act.

The provisions of Section 139 of Negotiable Instrument Act reads as under:-
139- Presumption in favour of holder - It should be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque, of the nature referred to in section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
13.

Hon'ble Supreme court in a decision reported in (2010) 11 SCC 411 between Rangappa V/s Sri Mohan has held that - C.C.No.19265/2025 The presumption mandated by Section 139 of the act does indeed include the existence of a legally enforceable debt or liability.

It is also observed that Section 139 of the Act is an example of a reverse onus clause that has been included in furtherance of the legislative objective of improving the credibility of negotiable instrument.

It is also held that in such a scenario, the test of proportionality should guide the construction and interpretation of reverse onus clauses and the defendant caused cannot be expected to discharge an unduly high slandered or proof.
14. Therefore in view of the principles laid down in these decisions the onus is on the accused to rebut the presumption under 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

The accused has not issued any M/S. Coevolve Estates, Private Limited vs Bhaskara T.V on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196582031/
5 reply at the initial stage at the time of service of the legal notice.

sentences.text: The accused has not contested the case to rebut the presumption and he came up with mutual understanding with the complainant to settle the dispute and payment of due amount in terms of memo of settlement.
Therefore there is no defence from the accused to rebut the presumption under Section 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

The complainant has produced the e certified copy of the sale deed as Ex.P.14 which shows that the cheques were issued towards payment of sale C.C.No.19265/2025 considaration and the undertaking letter given by the accused as Ex.P.15 shows he has sought time to arrange funds to clear the cheques.
These documents proves existance of legally recovarable debt and issuance of said cheques for lawful consideration.
As discussed above all the statutory requirements are complied.
The accused has failed to rebut the presumption under Section 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Therefore this court concludes that the complainant has successfully proved that the accused has committed the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Therefore this court answers the above point No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. POINT NO. 2 :
The complainant and the accused appeared before the court reporting amicable arrangement made by them to payment of due amount by the accused to the complainant and filed joint memo.
Under the joint memo, they have reported that the matter has been settled and they have entered into settlement for payment of Rs.1,18,37,500/- towards full and final settlement.
The accused agreed to pay said amount to the complainant either by way of DD or RTGS on or before 27.10.2025.
Both the complainant and accused have agreed that indefault to pay the amount as agreed in the joint memo the court can pass the judgment based on the joint memo.
It appears that the accused and complainant have voluntarily C.C.No.19265/2025 agreed for said settlement.

On 27-10-2025 both the complainant and accused appeared before the court and submitted that accused has not paid the amount as agreed in the joint memo and both of them have stated that the judgment may be passed by considering the joint memo.
Even in the absence of joint memo the complainant has independetly proved existance of considaration and issuance of cheque and all other statutory requirements under law.
Therefore the joint memo may be considered for awarding sentence.
Therefore this court answers the Point No. 2 in the Affirmative.
16. Point No.3 :

IN view of the findings on above point Nos.1 and 2, the court proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

By exercising powers conferred under Section 278(2) of Bharathiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita the accused is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act and he is sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.1,18,37,500/- (Rs.One Crore Eighteen Lakhs Thirty Seven Thousand & Five Hundred only),
In default to pay the fine, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment of 6 months.

Further by exercising powers conferred under Section 395(1)(b) of Bharathiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita a sum of Rs.1,18,37,500/- (Rs.One Crore Eighteen Lakhs Thirty Seven C.C.No.19265/2025 Thousand & Five Hundred only)/entire fine amount shall be paid as compensation to the complainant.
